title: Verified semantic retrieval
summary: Inspect a verified EngramPack semantic asset through exact bounded vector retrieval and a frozen-pack adapter. Queries are externally encoded canonical vectors, not natural-language prompts or a text encoder.

steps.explanation: Load a pack only after its manifest, canonical records, semantic metadata, and semantic tensor assets verify. The semantic component binds ordered record IDs to finite FP32 key and value matrices plus declared key/value encoder identities; key width, value width, and backbone hidden width are independent.
shapes: keys [M,K] and values [M,V] with ordered record_ids [M]
K key width, V value width, and D backbone hidden width are independently declared
observe: verified pack ID and semantic encoder identities
rejection before semantic arrays are used when verification, dimensions, or identities disagree

steps.explanation: Supply already encoded canonical query vectors. A query may be one vector per batch item and broadcast over positions, or one vector per batch-position; an optional mask has the matching batch or batch-position layout. Retrieval is exact raw-dot-product or cosine scoring as declared by the verified pack, with bounded top-K and comparisons.
observe: retrieval status: hit, unknown, temporal_miss, or conflict
trace fields including bounded candidate/comparison information and tie resolution

steps.explanation: Equal-score candidates are ordered deterministically by descending score then ascending record ID. A below-threshold query is unknown; a time filter is inclusive and reports temporal_miss when matching records exist but none are valid at the requested time. Distinct equal-score records remain an explicit conflict rather than an arbitrary winner.
shapes: one outcome per unmasked query position
ordered hits [top_k] with scalar score and value vector [V]
trace records status, ordered IDs, scores, and deterministic tie details
observe: stable record-ID ordering for equal scores
conflict status with top_k ordering and up to 16 deterministic tied IDs

steps.explanation: The adapter retains the verified retriever outside the model state dict, freezes retrieved key/value assets, projects V to D, and gates the projected residual with a trainable sigmoid gate. Replacing a retriever swaps only a verified matching pack; it does not alter adapter parameters. Frozen attachment comparisons disable gradients for the backbone and adapter and use inference mode.
shapes: frozen external keys [M,K] and values [M,V] are not model parameters
observe: frozen pack identity and no-gradient attachment state
gate and lookup diagnostics alongside retrieval status, record IDs, and scores

steps.explanation: A DenseLM names each semantic adapter and gives that adapter explicit ownership of one injection site: embedding, after_block at a zero-based block index, or final after final normalization. Multiple adapters and hybrid multipack attachments are explicit named attachments, not aliases for lexical memory placement; full-prefix and cached forwards must agree at supported sites for the same query.
shapes: one SemanticQueryBatch or encoder-SHA-256-keyed query mapping for multiple key spaces
observe: attachment name, site, and optional block index
per-attachment retrieval status, record IDs, scores, gate, and lookup diagnostics
failure-closed missing or mismatched query identities

steps.explanation: Toy worlds use deterministic structured-key and value encoders with declared identities. Producer facts are distinct from query/answer artifacts; each world has an isolated pack, and worlds share a canonical start key while intermediate and terminal assignments change. Held-out queries are also evaluated against another held-out world's pack to verify each task follows the attached assignment. Wording templates are partitioned, and multi-hop questions traverse one-edge records with no direct start-to-final shortcut. Correct, disabled, random, conflicting, and incomplete packs are frozen no-gradient attachment controls.
shapes: one-edge retrieved value vectors [B,T,V] per hop
per-task knowledge-swap ratio numerator and denominator are counts of changed-assignment queries
observe: world, wording, producer, and evaluation partition identities
per-hop trace record IDs, scores, statuses, and control-pack identity
knowledge-swap ratio or null with a zero-eligible-query reason

prerequisites: Use a semantic EngramPack whose records, semantic metadata, keys, and values have verified together; a records-only pack is not retrievable semantic memory.
Provide externally encoded canonical query vectors with the exact declared key encoder identity and width; this lesson does not encode natural-language prompts.
Use the Phase D semantic lesson scaffold, which prepares the required verified pack and canonical query artifacts rather than inventing vectors or encoder identities.
try_changes: Predict whether [B,K] or [B,T,K] queries produce broadcast or per-position retrieval, then inspect the trace.
Construct equal-score record IDs and confirm descending-score then ascending-record-ID order plus conflict status.
Compare a valid-as-of query with a below-threshold and an out-of-validity query; distinguish hit, unknown, and temporal_miss.
Attach correct, disabled, random, conflicting, and incomplete verified packs with all model parameters frozen; compare traces without gradients.
Attach two verified packs with distinct encoder SHA-256 identities and supply the keyed query mapping; then move one adapter between embedding, after_block, and final ownership.
limits: Externally encoded canonical vectors are not a natural-language encoder, parser, or evidence of natural-language understanding. Held-out prompt wording is a split check only.

Exact bounded retrieval establishes only the declared score, tie, threshold, temporal, and trace behavior for a verified pack; it does not certify pack truth, encoder semantics, source rights, answer quality, or speed.
Toy-world retrieval and frozen-pack comparisons do not establish open-world factual knowledge, language understanding, learned transfer, or production retrieval quality.

Knowledge-swap ratio is per task: changed-assignment queries whose retrieval follows the attached pack divided by eligible changed-assignment queries. It is null with an explicit reason when the denominator is zero.

papers.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.claim_boundary: This work motivates vector retrieval as a research question. SparseLab's lesson uses externally supplied canonical vectors and makes no claim to implement its text encoder, question answering protocol, or results.

papers.title: Memory Networks
papers.claim_boundary: This work motivates explicit memory interfaces. SparseLab only demonstrates verified bounded retrieval and an adapter under its declared toy-world protocol; it does not reproduce Memory Networks results.
